title: Can I SURVIVE Petrified Chess?
summary: Chess.com 'Petrified' variant vs higher-rated humans (goal: win 3). A non-pawn piece that makes a capture turns to stone on the square where it captured and becomes an immovable brick/wall; pawns never get petrified and may also step sideways (no sideways captures). Captures score points by the captured piece's value; most points wins at game end (e.g. threefold repetition), reaching 20 points auto-claims victory, checkmate still wins. He loses game 1 on points at a threefold repetition, then wins games 2-4 mostly by kingside mating attacks around the stone walls.
rules: Standard starting position and moves, except:

When a non-pawn piece (including the king) captures, it is petrified: it turns into a gray stone block on the capture square and can never move again (acts as a permanent obstacle that blocks both sides; it cannot be captured - inferred from 'brick'/'wall').
Pawns that capture are NOT petrified.
Pawns may additionally move one square sideways (left/right) but cannot capture sideways.
Each capture scores points for the capturer equal to the captured piece's value: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3-5 (narrator says 'bishops are also worth five' - ambiguous), rook 5, queen 9.
A player reaching 20 points automatically wins ('they need 20 to auto claim the victory').
If the game ends in a draw (e.g. threefold repetition), the player with more points wins.
Checkmate wins outright. Promoted pawns give no extra points (narrator's guess).
win_condition: Checkmate, or reach 20 points, or have more points when the game ends by repetition/draw; also on time.
